parts.title: My brother the champion
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
My older brother, Marek, is a professional gamer. When he told our parents that he wanted to play games for a living, they were not happy at all. My father said that it was a hobby, not a job, and my mother worried that he would never go out.

But Marek was serious. He practised for six hours every day after school, and he studied videos of the best players to learn their tricks. At sixteen, he joined a small team, and they travelled to a tournament in Berlin. They lost in the first round, and he cried all the way home.

He did not give up, though. A year later, his team won a national competition and received a prize of five thousand euros. Now my parents come to his matches and cheer louder than anyone.

I play too, but only for fun. Marek says that being a champion is hard work. He has to eat well, sleep eight hours and do exercise every morning, because it helps him think quickly. I think that the most important lesson he has taught me is that you must work hard to be good at anything.

questions.prompt: How did Marek's parents feel about his plan?
options: They did not like it at all
They were delighted at the idea
They did not care very much
questions.explanation: They were not happy at all.

questions.prompt: How did Marek improve his skills?
options: By watching videos of top players
questions.explanation: He studied videos of the best players to learn their tricks.

questions.prompt: What happened at the tournament in Berlin?
options: His team won the first round
His team lost in the first round
His team could not travel there
questions.explanation: They lost in the first round and he cried all the way home.

questions.prompt: How do the parents behave now?
options: They ask him to choose another job
They still worry about his health
They watch the matches and cheer
questions.explanation: They come to his matches and cheer louder than anyone.

questions.prompt: What lesson has the writer learned from her brother?
options: You should play for fun only
You must work hard to succeed
questions.explanation: You must work hard to be good at anything.

parts.title: A short history of video games
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
The first video games were very simple. In 1972, a game called Pong appeared in bars and shops. [1] Two players hit a small white ball across the screen with two white lines, and that was all.

During the 1980s, games moved into people's homes. [2] Families bought small machines that they could connect to the television and play in the living room.

In the 1990s, the pictures became much better. [3] Characters had more colours and movements, and some games had a story with music.

In the 2000s, the internet changed everything. [4] Players could now compete with friends or with people from the other side of the world.

Today, gaming is a huge industry, and millions of people play on their phones. [5] Some of them even earn their living by playing in competitions.
sentences: Soon, the number of players grew every year.
It was very easy to learn, but hard to stop playing.
Connecting to a game online was suddenly possible.
This made the games feel more like a real film.
Many of the early games were invented by students.
Others work in offices where they design new games.

gaps.explanation: It was very easy to learn describes Pong, and the next sentence explains what it was like.
The number of players grew soon after games moved into homes.
Better pictures make games feel more like a real film, and the next sentence talks about characters and story.
Connecting online became possible and so players could compete far away.
Others work in offices continues from the people who play for a living.

parts.title: Playing games safely
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Games are fun, but it is important to play them safely. First of all, do not play for [1] long without a break. Doctors say that you should stand up and move every hour. If you play online, never tell strangers [2] real name or your address. Some people are not kind, and they may try to make you angry. If that happens, you [3] leave the game and tell an adult. Also, remember that games are made to be hard to stop. Many players say, "Just [4] more minute," and then play for an hour. It is a good idea to decide how long you will play [5] you start. Then use an alarm to help you keep [6] your plan.

gaps.explanation: Too long means longer than is healthy without a break.
Your real name: possessive adjective for the reader.
The modal gives advice about what to do if someone is unkind.
One more minute is a common phrase.
Decide how long you will play before you start.
Keep to your plan means follow it.

parts.title: A talk about esports
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: esther
turns.text: Hello, everybody. Today, I would like to talk to you about esports, which means competitions in video games. In recent years, they have become very popular. Last year, more than five hundred million people around the world watched esports on their screens, and some matches were seen by more people than a big football final. The best players come from countries such as South Korea, China and the United States. They usually start young, and many of them stop playing professionally before they are thirty, because their reactions become slower. A top team practises for about ten hours a day, and it has a coach, a doctor and often a cook. The prizes can be very high. At one tournament, the winners shared more than thirty million dollars. However, the road to the top is hard, and only a few players succeed. If you want to try it yourself, the first step is to join a team at your school or in your town.

gaps.explanation: More than five hundred million people watched.

gaps.explanation: Players come from South Korea, China and the United States.

gaps.explanation: Many stop before they are thirty.

gaps.explanation: A top team practises for about ten hours a day.

gaps.prompt: The team has a coach, a doctor and a ___
gaps.explanation: It has a coach, a doctor and often a cook.

gaps.prompt: The first step is to join a ___

parts.title: An interview with a game designer
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Calum, you design video games for a living. How did you get started?

turns.speaker: g
turns.text: I made my first game at the age of fourteen, on my father's old computer. It was a very simple game about a frog crossing a road, but my friends loved it.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What does your team do every day?

turns.speaker: g
turns.text: We start with a meeting to see what has to be done. Then the artists draw the characters, the writers invent the story, and the programmers make everything work.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is the hardest part of making a game?

turns.speaker: g
turns.text: Testing. A game can have thousands of small problems, and we must find them all before the players do. Sometimes, we test one level for a month.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Where do your ideas come from?

turns.speaker: g
turns.text: Everywhere! From films, books, dreams and even from the bus journey to work. I always carry a small notebook in my pocket.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do you still have time to play games?

turns.speaker: g
turns.text: Of course. It is part of my job to try other games, but I also play board games with my family on Sundays.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What would you say to someone who wants to design games?

turns.speaker: g
turns.text: Start small and finish what you start. A short game that works is better than a huge game that you never complete.
